Themes

AI across modes

Answers that cross text, images, audio, clips and buttons, and the design work of letting information flow between them.

A recording, an image or a long document holds an enormous amount of decision-relevant information, but the cost of getting it out has always been too high. Multimodal AI changes that: it can read a frame, find the seconds that matter, and write an answer that mixes words, pictures and clips. The question that sits under every pattern in this theme is the one I get asked most at work: when an answer crosses text, images, clips and action buttons, how should that information flow?

14 patterns

  1. Ask, answer, check, decide

    Design the whole chain from a person's question to their decision as one flow. Break any link and trust in the AI is hollowed out.

    From Multimodal Alexa

    1. Ask
    2. Answer
    3. Check
    4. Decide
    • AI across modes

  2. Make the first question pay off

    When an AI needs to learn about a new user before it can help them, ask in a way that produces the first result on the spot, so the person gets value and the system gets context in the same minute.

    From Artist onboarding

    1. Ask
    2. Answer
    3. Check
    4. Decide
    • AI across modes

  3. Each choice narrows the next

    When a person gives the AI several inputs in a row, use each one to make the next easier to give, so the task gets lighter as the system learns.

    From Artist onboarding

    1. Ask
    2. Answer
    3. Check
    4. Decide
    • AI across modes

  4. Offer the questions it can answer

    Start from the evidence the AI actually has, generate the questions that evidence answers well, and offer those, instead of inviting any question and failing on the ones it cannot answer.

    From Multimodal Alexa

    1. Ask
    2. Answer
    3. Check
    4. Decide
    • AI across modes

  5. Index by what it covers

    Turn a long piece of content into a table of contents organized by the things in it, so a person can jump to the one they care about and skip the rest.

    From Product Jumplinks

    1. Ask
    2. Answer
    3. Check
    4. Decide
    • AI across modes
    • AI for accessibility

  6. Index by question

    Organize content by the questions a person actually has, not by the things in it or the order its author chose, and hand the content back to the reader's own priorities.

    From Topic Jumplinks

    1. Ask
    2. Answer
    3. Check
    4. Decide
    • AI across modes
    • AI for accessibility

  7. Say what it will make

    Before an AI produces something from a person's inputs, tell them what kind of thing is coming and how their inputs shape it, so the result is recognized rather than puzzled over.

    From Artist onboarding

    1. Ask
    2. Answer
    3. Check
    4. Decide
    • AI across modes

  8. Match the mode to the question

    Answer in a richer mode (a picture, a recording, a clip) only when it carries something text cannot. For a fact, text wins; for how something works or feels, showing beats telling.

    From Multimodal Alexa

    1. Ask
    2. Answer
    3. Check
    4. Decide
    • AI across modes
    • AI for accessibility

  9. Show the evidence behind the answer

    When an AI answers from a source, return the source with the answer, so the person can open it, read on, and check that it really says what the AI claims.

    From Multimodal Alexa, clip answers

    1. Ask
    2. Answer
    3. Check
    4. Decide
    • AI across modes

  10. When one answer may be wrong, offer a few

    If the AI cannot be sure its best answer is right, return a short ranked set rather than a single confident one, and make it easy to move to the next.

    From Multimodal Alexa

    1. Ask
    2. Answer
    3. Check
    4. Decide
    • AI across modes

  11. Say "I don't know"

    Decide, as a design matter, when the AI should answer with confidence and when it should admit it has nothing, because trust lives on the line between the two.

    From Multimodal Alexa, generated answers

    1. Ask
    2. Answer
    3. Check
    4. Decide

  12. Act where it appears

    When AI recognizes something inside a piece of content, put the action on that thing, at the moment it appears, so the content turns from display into something you can act on.

    From Video Hotspots, multimodal Alexa

    1. Ask
    2. Answer

  13. Make mistakes easy to catch

    Assume the AI will be wrong some of the time, and design so the person notices quickly and can push back with almost no effort.

    From Product Jumplinks, Topic Jumplinks, multimodal Alexa

    1. Ask
    2. Answer
    3. Check

    • AI for accessibility

  14. Structure is accessibility

    The structure AI adds to content so it can be asked is the same structure that makes it work without sound, without pictures or without a mouse. Build it as the foundation, not a patch.
